study type: Randomized Clinical Trial and Birth Cohort Study
exposure: Intermittent Prophylactic Treatment in Pregnancy (IPTp) with Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine (SP) or Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine (DP)
Maternal transfer of malaria-specific IgG sub-types to the fetus
Maternal Plasmodium falciparum infection during pregnancy
outcome: Cord levels of IgG sub-types (IgG1, IgG2, IgG3, IgG4) against P. falciparum specific antigens
Incidence of malaria in the first birth year of children
cohort: The study screened 637 cord blood samples from a Ugandan birth cohort of children born to mothers who had Plasmodium falciparum infection during pregnancy.
finding: Malaria prophylaxis in pregnant mothers using DP or SP did not affect cord blood antibody expression against P. falciparum specific antigens, and these antibodies did not protect against malaria in the first year of life; conversely, poverty and maternal malaria during pregnancy were identified as key risk factors for infant malaria infections.
